title: Optimization of an erythroid culture system to reduce the cost of in vitro production of red blood cells
author: Poldee, Metheetrairut, et al.

steps.title: Collect LRS cones
steps.instruction: Obtain Leucocyte Reduction System (LRS) cones from healthy donors (n = 3 per experiment) with informed consent and IRB approval.

steps.title: Dilute blood and set density gradient
steps.instruction: Dilute each blood sample with Hanks’ Balanced Salt Solution (HBSS) containing 0.6 % (v/v) citrate dextrose solution (ACD), then layer onto Ficoll‑Histopaque‑1077 and centrifuge at 400 g for 30 min at 20 °C.

steps.title: Harvest and wash mononuclear cells
steps.instruction: Collect the mononuclear cell layer at the interface, wash 2–4 times with HBSS + 0.6 % ACD to remove platelet clumps.

steps.title: Lyse residual red cells
steps.instruction: Incubate the washed cells in pre‑warmed red‑cell lysis buffer (150 mM NH₄Cl, 1 mM EDTA·2H₂O, 10 mM KHCO₃, pH 7.5 adjusted with NaOH) for 12 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash and resuspend in cold MACS buffer
steps.instruction: Wash cells again with HBSS + 0.6 % ACD, then pool into cold MACS buffer (0.5 % BSA, 0.6 % CPD in 1× PBS) and centrifuge at 400 g for 5 min at 20 °C.

steps.title: Label CD34+ cells with magnetic beads
steps.instruction: After discarding supernatant, add 500 µL MACS buffer, 100 µL MACS‑Fc blocking agent, and 100 µL MACS‑CD34 beads (sufficient for up to 1 × 10⁸ cells) to the pellet; incubate at 4 °C for 30 min with constant mixing on a roller.

steps.title: Magnetic separation of CD34+ cells
steps.instruction: Apply the cell suspension to an LS column, wash the column with cold MACS buffer, elute cells with cold MACS buffer, then transfer to an MS column; pass 1.5 mL MACS buffer through the MS column and collect the CD34⁺ cells in 1 mL MACS buffer.
